    Processors


    Your CPU is the beating heart of your gaming PC. This is why Overclockers UK's extensive range of AMD and Intel processors are built from the ground up to offer the best possible performance in the latest AAA games and work applications, no matter your budget. What’s more, you can choose from a selection of entry-level, mid-range, and high-end processors or even opt for extreme CPUs, such as an AMD Threadripper or Intel Xeon.


    Extreme CPUs

    Intel Xeon and AMD Threadripper processors are the extreme of the extreme, offering unparalleled core counts – they're a great solution for professionals and servers. They can handle super complex tasks and tackle many tasks simultaneously.

    Thermal Compounds

    When it’s time to build from scratch or give your PC a spring clean, you’ll want some thermal compound to apply between the CPU and the cooler. This helps to create an efficient transfer of heat from the processor’s IHS (integrated heat spreader) and your cooler’s base plate.

    CPU Bundles

    We’ve paired together some of the most popular CPUs with motherboards and RAM that we believe offer stellar performance time after time, taking the guesswork out of your build – and even better, they’re discounted!


    Want to Read More?

    Installing your new CPU is one of the most important steps in building your gaming PC. In this guide on the Overclockers UK Blog, we’ve covered everything you need to know.

    Read More

    Processors FAQ


    What is a processor, and why is it important for my PC?

    A processor, or Central Processing Unit (CPU), serves as your gaming PC's brain, executing instructions and performing calculations essential for tasks; its importance lies in influencing overall system speed, and multitasking capabilities.

    What is the difference between Intel Core i3, i5, i7, and i9 processors?

    Core i3 processors are generally entry-level, i5 CPUs are a great choice for most gamers, with Intel i7 and i9 CPUs offering the most performance and designed for enthusiast gaming or streaming.

    Does my CPU have graphics?

    Some processors include integrated graphics, allowing you to work and even play some basic games without needing a GPU. To find out if you have integrated graphics, check your manufacturer documentation.
